candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Africa TTS

Text-to-speech for **92 African languages and English**, with voice cloning, built on
[Kyutai's Pocket TTS](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts). Every language has a default
voice, so all you need is text and a language code.

🎙️ [**Try it live**](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AfriSpeech/africa-tts-demo) ·
🔊 [Samples](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AfriSpeech/africa-tts-samples) ·
🤗 [Model](https://huggingface.co/AfriSpeech/africa-tts)

> An ongoing project: native-speaker feedback is what improves it most. See
> [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## ⚡ Fast and high-fidelity speech on CPU, no GPU needed

**Africa TTS runs on PyTorch (fp32 unquantised) by default: fast, full-fidelity audio without
quantization degradation, faster than real time on an ordinary CPU.** On a 4-vCPU cloud machine it speaks 2.4×
faster than real time ([speed benchmark](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md#speed)).
It also runs on an NVIDIA GPU with `device="cuda"`.

## 🎯 Intelligible

On held-out sentences transcribed by Omnilingual ASR, Africa TTS is more intelligible than
MMS-TTS in 21 of 27 languages. The 813M OmniVoice, seven times its size, is more intelligible in
24 of 29, by small margins:
[benchmark](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md#intelligibility).

## Install

```bash
pip install africa-tts
```

English also needs espeak-ng (`apt install espeak-ng` / `brew install espeak-ng`). The first time,
it asks before downloading the model (about 440 MB) from Hugging Face, then caches it and works
offline. In scripts, approve the download with `--yes`, `AfricaTTS.load(download=True)`, or
`africa-tts --download` beforehand. On a CPU-only Linux machine, you can install the CPU build of
PyTorch with `pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu africa-tts`.

## Use

```bash
africa-tts "Akwaaba! Yɛfrɛ me Kofi." --lang twi -o twi.wav
africa-tts --list-languages
africa-tts serve                       # the API server below, on port 8000
```

```python
from africa_tts import AfricaTTS

tts = AfricaTTS.load()                                                  # PyTorch, CPU (default)
audio = tts.generate("Akwaaba! Yɛfrɛ me Kofi.", lang="twi")              # default Twi voice
audio = tts.generate("Hello Ghana!", lang="eng", voice="my_voice.wav")  # clone a 3-10 s clip
tts.save(audio, "out.wav")

You see what the copilot sees, approve what it plans, and keep both hands in Blender the entire time.

| AI chat in a detached browser tab | One companion window beside your viewport |

candidates.readme_excerpt:
T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` |

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). # Pi Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own. Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other way around. Customize Pi with [extensions](packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md), [skills](packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md), [prompt templates](packages/coding-agent/docs/prompt-templates.md), and [themes](packages/coding-agent/docs/themes.md). Bundle them as [Pi packages](packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md) and share via npm or git. Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode. Ask Pi to build what you want, or install a package that does it your way. Use Pi [interactively](packages/coding-agent/docs/usage.md), automate it in [print or JSON mode](packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md), control it over [RPC](packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md), or build apps with the [Pi TypeScript SDK](packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md). See [OpenClaw](https://github.com/OpenClaw/OpenClaw) for a real-world integration. ## Getting started Install the command-line interface: ```bash curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows: ```shell powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The installer pins all dependencies and updates Pi with `pi update`. Alternatively, install directly with npm, which does not pin transitive dependencies: ```bash npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ``` Pi requires Node.js 22.19 or newer. The macOS, Linux, and Windows installers can install it if needed. Pi does not require dependency lifecycle scripts for a normal npm installation.
